message.content:
The most recent common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of the two major mammalian clades that give rise to them: **Carnivora** (the order that contains lions) and **Perissodactyla** (the order that contains zebras).  

In phylogenetic terms, this ancestor lies at the base of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which includes all placental mammals that evolved on the northern supercontinent Laurasia. It is the last common ancestor of the entire Laurasiatherian lineage, from which the separate lineages leading to carnivores (Felidae, etc.) and odd‑toed ungulates (Equidae, etc.) diverged.
